sources.title: Kumar et al., Functional domains of the human estrogen receptor
sources.depth: Primary PubMed abstract read in the accessible rendered record.
sources.supports: Hormone-binding and DNA/nuclear-binding regions participate in estrogen-responsive transcription in tested systems.
sources.limits: No full manuscript or study figure inspected; no universal receptor location, all-gene direction or clinical response claim.

sources.title: Giangrande et al., Mapping functional domains of progesterone-receptor isoforms
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved and read through PubMed search text. Direct PubMed opens returned empty/error results.
sources.supports: Distinct human PR forms regulate progesterone-responsive transcription differently in defined cell contexts.
sources.limits: Abstract depth only. No full paper/figure, universal PR-A/PR-B direction, hormone administration or patient-benefit inference.

sources.title: Ogiso et al., Human EGF–EGFR extracellular complex
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved and read through PubMed search text; direct record open did not provide an article body.
sources.supports: EGF binding to EGFR extracellular regions and receptor-mediated partnership in a defined 2:2 structural complex.
sources.limits: No source figure or manuscript inspected. The cartoon is original, not a structural reproduction or universal two-ligand requirement.

sources.title: Zhang et al., Allosteric EGFR kinase activation
sources.depth: Primary abstract read in the accessible rendered PubMed record.
sources.supports: An interacting asymmetric kinase-domain arrangement can couple receptor partnership to activation.
sources.limits: Full text/figures not inspected. The two generic cartoon lobes compress the interaction; they do not establish atomic geometry, activation-loop phosphorylation or a complete growth pathway.

sources.title: Freeman et al., PD-1 engagement by PD-L1 and lymphocyte regulation
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved and read through PubMed search text. PMC full-text route returned a browser challenge; alternate XML and PubMed routes returned errors.
sources.supports: PD-L1 can engage PD-1 and reduce activation-related lymphocyte proliferation/cytokine responses in tested systems.
sources.limits: No full article or source figure inspected. No complete shutdown, universal exhaustion, exclusive tumor PD-L1, drug ranking or clinical benefit claim.

sources.title: Park et al., FAP as a dual-specificity cell-surface serine protease
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved and read through PubMed search text.
sources.supports: Natural/recombinant FAP enzymatic activity and cell-surface serine-protease identity.
sources.limits: No full article/figure or therapeutic efficacy data inspected. Does not imply FAP is a signaling receptor or that binding it is tumor-exclusive/safe.

sources.title: IUPAC medicinal-chemistry definitions: agonist and antagonist
sources.depth: Official full HTML definition entries for agonist and antagonist read. This is primary nomenclature guidance, not an experimental paper.
sources.supports: Agonism initiates receptor-characteristic response; antagonism opposes receptor-associated agonist responses.
sources.limits: Does not classify every ligand or prove clinical efficacy. The separate guide-to-pharmacology PDF route redirected to login and was not counted as access.

sources.title: Diwanji et al., HER2–HER3–NRG1β complex
sources.depth: Existing lesson citation was refreshed at primary abstract and accessible record-text depth; figure-caption text was returned but source-figure pixels/full manuscript were not inspected.
sources.supports: Preserved distinction between ligand binding and HER2–HER3 partnership, including singly liganded complex.
sources.limits: Existing no-known-direct-HER2-ligand teaching is retained; the new figure depicts EGFR rather than a HER2 ligand. No treatment or mutation-response claim adopted.
